display.title: Episode 35: Shoot Bullets in the Jacket Too
display.summary_short: Pot-lid drums for the march, and the story of a tzedakah collector who tricks an armed robber into emptying his gun, plus a long-awaited letter in the mailbox.
display.summary_long: A summer show from 1982. Uncle Yossi opens with news of the Tzivos Hashem Club and the new children's Sefer Torah, inviting listeners to call or write to get a letter. A listener's letter about drumming on a pot lid during the march leads into a lively march with make-believe drums (with Mommy's permission). Story time: Reb Nachman, a poor woodcutter who collects and distributes tzedakah, is held up by a robber with a gun who takes the tzedakah money. A young Tzivos Hashem member leads the Shema in Studio 604. Then Reb Nachman asks the robber to shoot holes in his jacket and hat so the poor will believe him, until the gun is empty and he can grab back the money. Uncle Yossi quotes Shlomo HaMelech, 'tzedakah saves from death'. The mailbox brings a colorful letter from a yeshiva boy whose whole street listens to the show, and the program ends with a summer reminder: no vacation from davening, learning Torah and giving tzedakah every day.
display.lesson: Guard tzedakah money as a sacred trust, and keep up davening, Torah learning and tzedakah every day, even on vacation.

date.note: Week after episode 34 (7 Av 5742); a letter dated March 3 is read 'five months' later (March to July); summer vacation.

advisories.note: An armed robber threatens the hero's life and fires his gun at the jacket and hat.
